36 Four potential divider circuits each consist of a battery of electromotive force (e.m.f.) 9 V and
negligible internal resistance connected to a combination of resistors. Each of the resistors in the
circuits has a resistance of X or 2X.
Which circuit has the largest output voltage V ?

hints: Notice in each diagram which resistor or parallel combination V is taken across - the lower part between the middle junction and the $9\text{ V}$ negative terminal.
Recall the potential divider rule that the share of $9\text{ V}$ across a part is proportional to its resistance: $V_{out}=9 \times R_{lower}/R_{total}$.
Compare the fraction $R_{lower}/R_{total}$ for $X$ and $2X$ combinations, including $X$ in parallel with $2X$, to see which gives the largest lower resistance share.
walkthrough: Identify that the $9\text{ V}$ battery with negligible internal resistance is fully applied across the series combination, and V is the p.d. across the lower section in each circuit.
Use $V = 9 \times R_{lower}/(R_{upper}+R_{lower})$, where parallel resistors must first be combined with $1/R_p = 1/R_1+1/R_2$.
For A: $R_{lower}=X$, $R_{total}=2X$, so $V=9 \times X/2X = 4.5\text{ V}$. For B: $R_{lower}=2X$, $R_{total}=3X$, so $V=9 \times 2X/3X = 6.0\text{ V}$.
For C: lower $R_p = X \times 2X/(X+2X)=2X/3$, total $=5X/3$, so $V=9 \times (2X/3)/(5X/3)=3.6\text{ V}$. For D: upper $R_p=2X/3$, lower $=X$, total $=5X/3$, so $V=9 \times X/(5X/3)=5.4\text{ V}$.
Comparing $4.5\text{ V}$, $6.0\text{ V}$, $3.6\text{ V}$ and $5.4\text{ V}$, the largest V is from the circuit with $X$ on top and $2X$ below. This is option B.

A.explanation: V is across the lower $X$ with total $X+X=2X$, so $V=9 \times X/2X=4.5\text{ V}$.

B.explanation: V is across the larger lower resistor $2X$ with total $3X$, so $V=9 \times 2X/3X=6.0\text{ V}$, the largest value.

C.explanation: The lower part is $X$ in parallel with $2X$, giving less than $X$, so V is less than half of $9\text{ V}$, about $3.6\text{ V}$.

D.explanation: The upper part is $X$ in parallel with $2X$, so the lower $X$ takes more than half of $9\text{ V}$, $5.4\text{ V}$, but less than circuit B.
